source_snapshot.evidence_note: Source retrieval and internal finite computations are not external proof validation or priority review.

claims.statement: For a finite rooted tree with q=4 symmetric Potts edge channels and selected independent q-symmetric sensors represented as attached noisy edges ending in perfectly observed terminals, the max-ray weighted-flow capacity is exactly computed by S_v = sum_child Phi_lambda(S_w) + sum_local_sensor g(rho), where Phi_lambda(S)=lambda^2*S/sqrt(1+(1-lambda^4)*S^2) and g(rho)=rho^2/sqrt(1-rho^4), with stated zero/one endpoint conventions.
assumptions: known edge and sensor parameters in [0,1]
nonnegative conserved flow allowed to terminate at sensor terminals
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact finite variational recursion; no external proof review
claims.novelty_boundary: This is the direct finite-tree p=3 nonlinear-capacity recursion; do not claim a novel general capacity algorithm.
claims.costs: O(|E|) scalar recursion for a fixed sensor set, plus real/integer arithmetic precision; supplied channels are not calibrated for free.
claims.falsifier: A finite tree and rational channel fixture where direct minimax-flow optimization disagrees with the recurrence or its extracted flow violates the path-energy bound.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review and exact-rational fixture audit; compare against standard nonlinear-capacity recursions.

claims.statement: For finite sensor menus with positive integer costs and budget B, a tree knapsack/convolution DP maximizes the finite capacity certificate; baseline scalar arithmetic work is O(B*sum_v menu_size(v)+B^2*|E|). Integer fixed-scale downward rounding returns a certified lower capacity bound using exact integer square roots.
claims.status: algorithm implemented and finite fixture passed; pseudo-polynomial complexity proof direct, but this optimizes a capacity certificate only
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite DP is a computational corollary of the capacity recursion. It is not a Bayes-optimal sensor-placement algorithm.
claims.costs: O(B^2|E|+B*number_of_sensor_options) transitions; integer bit complexity depends on Q and rational input bit lengths; rational budget scaling can inflate B.
claims.falsifier: An exhaustive finite menu instance where the DP value is below a feasible design's capacity or its selected set does not maximize the computed capacity objective.
claims.next_gate: Add a separately audited flow witness extractor and benchmark against exact outcome enumeration on small trees.

claims.statement: Conditional on the Astra-derived heterogeneous q=4 weighted-flow theorem and its exact posterior-cone dependency, any infinite-tree level-n boundary flow of mass b with max path energy at most one yields E[TV(root posterior,uniform)] >= b/(1600*sqrt(b^2+2)) and four-class MAP advantage >= b/(4800*sqrt(b^2+2)) for every n. A finite sensor menu inherits the bound for its full report record by extending sensor outputs along deterministic lambda=1 edges to a common level.
assumptions: independent ferromagnetic q=4 Potts channels on all ordinary and sensor edges
a feasible positive finite max-ray flow
posterior-cone proposition and heterogeneous weighted-flow proof are valid
claims.status: conditional internal theorem candidate; source-cone finite certificate replay is partly source-reported and not externally validated
claims.novelty_boundary: The released N49 capacity manuscript proves only homogeneous 0<lambda<1 and bounded outdegree. Heterogeneous edge channels, arbitrary locally finite degree, and this explicit constant come from an internal Astra derivation conditional on the cone input.
claims.costs: Channels/topology supplied or calibrated; finite BP O(|E|) four-vector updates; calibration and communication costs are separate; constant is weak and no physical validation exists.
claims.falsifier: Under independently verified q-symmetric channels and a correct positive-flow certificate, held-out E[TV] below the bound would refute the theorem/interface or its implementation.
claims.next_gate: Independent mathematical review of the full heterogeneous proof and rerun both long exact product-certificate traversals; then preregister a bounded-depth q=4 emulator test.

claims.statement: Capacity-optimal sensor selection need not maximize exact Bayes MAP success: at a single q=4 root, a cost-2 portfolio of one P_0.7 sensor has capacity 0.5621055 and MAP success 31/40, while two independent P_0.6 sensors have capacity 0.7717436 and MAP success 7/10.
assumptions: independent symmetric Potts reports conditional on root
claims.status: exact rational counterexample for MAP values plus deterministic numeric capacity calculation
claims.novelty_boundary: This blocks an overclaim about the DP objective; it does not establish hardness of Bayes-optimal sensor design.
claims.costs: Exact MAP enumeration checks 4^2 report tuples; capacity values use float output for display and can also be lower-bounded with integer Q arithmetic.
claims.falsifier: A correction to the exact q=4 outcome enumeration or the capacity recursion showing the stated portfolio ordering is wrong.
claims.next_gate: Keep certificate-optimal and Bayes-optimal design objectives separate; use exact finite enumeration as the comparator on test networks.

claims.statement: The pinned OpenAI/math N49 manuscript's stated model uses one common known 0<lambda<1 on every edge of a deterministic rooted tree with a uniform finite outdegree bound; it does not state the arbitrary edge-varying theorem in the Astra N49 card.
assumptions: source text interpreted at pinned OpenAI/math commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a
claims.status: source-reported primary-manuscript scope, independently checked against its abstract and theorem statement
claims.novelty_boundary: This prevents attributing the internal heterogeneous extension to the release paper.
claims.falsifier: A theorem statement in the pinned manuscript that quantifies independent lambda_e or removes its fixed degree bound.
claims.next_gate: Retain separate citation/status for the internal Astra extension.

claims.statement: Exact upward q=4 Potts belief propagation computes the root posterior on a finite tree with O(|E|) four-vector updates; expected Bayes success for an enumerated finite observation alphabet is (1/4)*sum_y max_i P(y|root=i).
claims.status: standard sum-product identity; finite script covers only the root-local exact MAP counterexample, not a general BP software package
claims.novelty_boundary: Do not claim BP, tree posterior computation, or exact MAP as a new result.
claims.costs: O(|E|) scalar-vector updates per sample; exact rational bit sizes depend on the full input description; finite-bit distributed messages need separate error bounds.
claims.falsifier: A finite tree fixture where the messages disagree with exhaustive joint enumeration under the declared conditional-independence model.
claims.next_gate: Implement full exact BP enumeration only if needed for a small emulator; audit quantized communication separately.
